questions: What is the initial value of the grid cell (sh, sw) before any moves are made?
Can Takahashi start on the boundary of the grid such that some directions are invalid for the first move?
Is it guaranteed that Takahashi will never attempt to move outside the bounds of the grid during any of the Q operations?
How exactly should the "modulo" operation be applied? Specifically, what is the modulus used for the final result?
Are all values of A_{h,w} guaranteed to be less than the modulus before and after each update?
Does the path count include all possible paths from (1,1) to (H,W), or only those satisfying additional constraints?
When printing the results, should each line contain just the numerical result or must it follow a specific format like "ans = X"?
What happens if a move would place Takahashi outside the grid boundaries—is this considered undefined behavior or explicitly disallowed?
answers: The cell has its given value from the input grid.
Takahashi can start anywhere within bounds; his moves are always valid.
Yes. All provided moves keep Takahashi within the grid boundaries.
The result must be printed modulo 998244353.
Grid values are less than 998244353; use modulo reduction in final output.
Yes. There are exactly C(H+W-2, H-1) valid paths between (1,1) and (H,W) under the defined movement rules.
Output just the numerical result on each line.
All provided moves keep Takahashi within bounds; this situation does not occur.
inline_prompts:
There is an H \times W grid. Let (h,w) denote the cell at the h-th row from the top and the w-th column from the left. A non-negative integer A_{h,w} is written in cell (h,w). The cell has its given value from the input grid. Takahashi starts at cell (sh,sw) and will perform Q changes to the grid. The i-th change is given by a character d_i (d_i is one of L, R, U, D) and a non-negative integer a_i, meaning Takahashi will do the following:
- Move one cell in the direction d_i. That is, if d_i is L, move left; if R, move right; if U, move up; if D, move down by one cell. Then, let the destination cell be (h,w), and set A_{h,w} to a_i.
After each change, print the answer to the following problem:
A sequence of cells P = ((h_1,w_1), \ldots, (h_{M},w_{M})) is said to be a path if and only if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- (h_1,w_1) = (1,1), (h_{M},w_{M}) = (H,W), and M = H + W - 1.
- For every i with 1 \leq i \leq M-1, either (h_{i+1}, w_{i+1}) = (h_i + 1, w_i) or (h_{i+1}, w_{i+1}) = (h_i, w_i + 1).
For a path P = ((h_1,w_1), \ldots, (h_{M},w_{M})), define f(P) = \prod_{1\leq i\leq M}A_{h_i,w_i}. Print the sum, modulo, of f(P) over all paths P.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
A_{1,1} \cdots A_{1,W}
\vdots
A_{H,1} \cdots A_{H,W}
Q sh sw
d_1 a_1
\vdots
d_Q a_Q
Output
Print Q lines.
The i-th line should contain the sum, modulo, of f(P) over all paths P after performing the i-th change to the grid.
Constraints
- 2 \leq H, W \leq 200000
- HW \leq 200000
- 0 \leq A_{h,w} < 998244353
- 1 \leq Q \leq 200000
